# **What Is a Vanity Phone Number? Complete 2026 Guide for Businesses & Personal Brands**

A vanity phone number is a phone number deliberately chosen for its memorability, visual impact, or brand alignment rather than being randomly assigned by a carrier. In 2026, it remains one of the most cost-effective tools for increasing call volume, strengthening local presence, and turning a simple contact detail into a lasting marketing asset.

At NumberGuy, we specialize in helping businesses, creators, and individuals own these numbers outright. This guide explains exactly what vanity numbers are, the main types that perform best, how ownership works, who benefits most, and how to acquire one that fits your goals.

## **Why Memorability Still Matters in 2026**

Phone numbers have not disappeared. They appear on Google Business Profiles, vehicle wraps, yard signs, radio spots, podcasts, Instagram bios, business cards, invoices, and referral conversations. When a prospect sees or hears a number once and can still recall it later, response rates climb.

Random numbers require effort to remember. A patterned or local vanity number reduces that friction. Research across advertising and local service industries consistently shows that easy-to-recall numbers generate higher inbound call volume than ordinary lines. For small and mid-sized businesses that rely on phone leads, this difference compounds over years of marketing spend.

Voice search, smart speakers, and AI assistants have not eliminated the need for strong numbers. They have simply shifted emphasis toward numbers that are easy to say out loud and easy to type into a phone. A clean repeating pattern or a familiar local area code performs well in both visual and audio contexts.

## **The Five Main Types of Vanity Phone Numbers**

Most valuable vanity numbers fall into one or more of these practical categories. The strongest inventory usually combines two or more traits.

1. **Spelled-Word (Alphanumeric) Numbers** These map letters on a phone keypad to form a word or short phrase (for example, numbers that spell CALL, ROOF, LAW, or a brand name). They excel in radio, podcast, and spoken advertising because the listener hears a word instead of a string of digits. They remain popular for national brands and certain local service categories.
2. **Repeating-Digit Numbers** Patterns such as endings in 7777, 8888, 9999, or triple repeats create instant visual and auditory recognition. These numbers look clean on signs and business cards and are easy to dictate over the phone. Cultural associations (lucky sevens, prosperous eights) add extra appeal for many buyers.
3. **Sequential Numbers** Ascending or descending sequences (1234, 2345, 9876) are processed by the brain as a single chunk rather than four separate digits. This makes them highly memorable after limited exposure and consistently among the most requested patterns.
4. **Pattern and Pair Numbers** These include mirrored patterns (1221), alternating pairs (1212 or 3434), or other structured digit arrangements. They offer strong visual symmetry and are often easier to remember than purely random endings while remaining more available than pure repeating blocks.
5. **Strong Local Area-Code Numbers** Sometimes the area code itself carries the branding power. A 212 in Manhattan, 310 in West Los Angeles, 404 in Atlanta, 305 in Miami, or 312 in Chicago signals local presence and established status. Pairing a respected area code with even a modest pattern creates a powerful combination for local businesses and real-estate professionals.

The most desirable numbers in any catalog typically blend a desirable area code with a clean repeating, sequential, or patterned ending.

## **A Brief History: From Utility to Brand Asset**

The North American Numbering Plan (NANP) began in 1947, creating the familiar 10-digit format still used across the United States, Canada, and parts of the Caribbean. For decades, phone numbers functioned purely as routing tools.

The commercial value of memorable numbers emerged with the growth of radio and television advertising. Classic examples such as 1-800-FLOWERS demonstrated that a number people could remember after hearing it once generated measurable results. As mobile phones, smartphones, and later voice assistants arrived, the market expanded beyond toll-free spelled words into local patterned numbers that work equally well on signage and in conversation.

Local Number Portability (LNP) rules, standardized by the FCC, made it possible for businesses and individuals to keep these numbers when changing carriers. That portability turned selected numbers into transferable assets rather than temporary assignments.

## **How Vanity Numbers Work Technically**

A vanity number is still a standard NANP 10-digit telephone number. There is no separate technology layer that makes a number “vanity.” The distinction lies in selection and ownership.

Behind the scenes, numbers are administered through the FCC’s Local Number Portability framework. When you buy a number from a provider such as NumberGuy, you receive the right to port that number to a compatible wireless carrier, landline provider, or interconnected VoIP platform. Once ported, the number routes through the new carrier’s network exactly like any other line.

The critical business distinction is ownership model:

- **Leasing / subscription model**: Many traditional providers retain control of the underlying assignment. You pay monthly fees to use the number. If payments stop, the number typically returns to the provider.
- **Outright ownership model**: You pay once, receive transfer documentation, and port the number to the carrier or VoIP system of your choice. Ongoing costs are limited to whatever your chosen service provider charges for the line itself. NumberGuy operates on this ownership model.

## **Who Benefits Most from Vanity Phone Numbers**

**Local service businesses** Contractors, roofers, plumbers, HVAC companies, landscapers, movers, and cleaning services rely heavily on phone leads generated by truck wraps, yard signs, door hangers, and Google Business Profiles. A memorable local number increases the chance that a prospect who sees the number once will actually call later.

**Real estate agents and teams** Agents live on referrals, listing packets, open-house signs, and repeat recognition. A strong local area code combined with a clean pattern reinforces professional presence across every marketing surface.

**Restaurants, hospitality, and event businesses** Menus, delivery apps, reservation cards, and social posts all benefit from numbers that customers can recall without searching.

**Professional services** Law firms, medical and dental practices, financial advisors, and consultants use vanity numbers on letterhead, websites, and advertising to project permanence and polish.

**Creators, coaches, and personal brands** Podcasters, course creators, consultants, and independent professionals treat their phone number as part of their public identity. A deliberate number signals intentionality in a way a random mobile number does not.

**Individuals and gift buyers** Some people simply want a clean personal number or a meaningful gift for a graduate, new business owner, or family member launching a venture. A one-of-a-kind patterned number can serve as both a practical tool and a lasting keepsake.

## **Lease Versus Own: The Decision That Defines Long-Term Value**

Most search results for vanity numbers lead to subscription platforms. Monthly fees of $10–$50 (or more when bundled with service) add up quickly. Over five years a $25 monthly number costs $1,500; over ten years it costs $3,000—and the buyer still does not own the asset.

Outright ownership inverts that equation. A one-time purchase in the range commonly offered by NumberGuy removes the recurring seller fee. The only ongoing cost is the standard monthly charge from whatever carrier or VoIP provider you choose. For any business or brand that expects to use the same contact number for more than two or three years, ownership usually delivers clearer long-term economics and greater control.

Ownership also means the number travels with you. Change carriers, switch VoIP platforms, or restructure your phone system—the number remains yours as long as you maintain service with a compatible provider.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

**Is a vanity phone number the same as a toll-free number?**

No. Toll-free numbers (800, 888, etc.) are non-geographic. Local vanity numbers use standard geographic area codes and often carry stronger local branding power for many businesses.

**Can I port a vanity number to any carrier?**

In the vast majority of cases, yes. FCC Local Number Portability rules require carriers and interconnected VoIP providers to facilitate valid port requests. Compatibility is high across major wireless, landline, and VoIP platforms.

**How long does porting take?**

Simple wireless-to-wireless ports frequently complete within one business day. Landline or more complex ports can take several business days. Accurate account information dramatically reduces delays.

**Do I need to keep paying NumberGuy after purchase?**

No. NumberGuy’s model is one-time purchase. After you receive the transfer kit and port the number, ongoing costs come only from the carrier or VoIP provider you select.

**Are vanity numbers still effective with smartphones and apps?**

Yes. Numbers continue to appear across high-visibility offline and online surfaces. Easy recall still converts casual exposure into actual phone calls.

**Can a vanity number be used as a personal line?**

Absolutely. Many individuals and personal brands use patterned or local numbers for professional identity, side businesses, or simply cleaner personal contact details.

They fall into two main categories: **toll-free vanity numbers** (800, 888, 877, 866, 855, 844, 833 prefixes) and **local vanity numbers** that incorporate your area code.

The psychology behind vanity numbers is simple yet powerful—human brains process words and patterns more easily than random number sequences. ## What is a US vanity number?

**A US vanity phone number transforms standard numeric digits into memorable words or phrases** using the traditional telephone keypad mapping system. These custom numbers replace forgettable digit sequences with brandable words like 1-800-FLOWERS or 1-888-GOT-JUNK, making them significantly easier for customers to remember, and dial. The magic happens through the **alphanumeric keypad correspondence** where each number (2-9) represents multiple letters. For example, pressing “2” corresponds to A, B, or C, while “3” represents D, E, or F. This system allows businesses to spell out their company name, service, or compelling call-to-action directly within their phone number.

Vanity numbers operate on **toll-free prefixes** (800, 888, 877, 866, 855, 844, 833) or local area codes, functioning exactly like traditional phone numbers while delivering enhanced marketing power. The key advantage lies in their memorability—customers can instantly recall 1-800-PLUMBER far more easily than remembering 1-800-758-6237.

These numbers serve dual purposes: **immediate brand recognition and long-term customer retention**. It has been conclusively established that the response rate is nearly 30 percent higher if your trade advertisement carries a toll-free number. By mentioning a toll-free number, your business may appear like a major corporation to clients which will prompt him/her to call you immediately.

By offering a toll-free number, you are creating an opportunity for customers to call you without having to pay. This encourages potential customers to call you and eventually place orders over phone repeatedly. Thus toll-free numbers are a powerful and cost-effective marketing tool.

### [The Benefits of Owning a Vanity Phone Number](https://numberguy.com/the-benefits-of-owning-a-vanity-phone-number/)

**Published:** December 6, 2024
**Author:** NGAdmin

**Content:**

![Numberguy   Number Guy   Buy Vanity Phone Number Buy Vanity Number at Numberguy](https://NumberGuy.com/wp-content/uploads/numberguy-9-207x300.png "Numberguy - Number Guy - Buy Vanity Phone Number Buy Vanity Number at Numberguy")

Owning a [vanity phone number](https://numberguy.com/ "vanity phone number") can offer a multitude of benefits for businesses of all sizes. Let’s break down why these numbers are such valuable assets:

**Memorable Contact Point:** A vanity number serves as an easy-to-remember contact point. When potential customers only need to remember a sequence that spells out a word or a straightforward series of numbers, the likelihood of them calling increases. Think about it: which number is easier to remember, 1-800-PAINT or 1-800-724-6837?

**Enhanced Credibility:** A vanity number can also enhance the credibility of your business. A number that aligns well with your business’s services or products can create an image of stability and professionalism. It’s akin to wearing a tailored suit to a business meeting—it sets the tone before you even speak.

**Streamlined Marketing:** Incorporating a vanity number into your marketing materials can streamline your campaigns. Instead of hoping customers will remember a random set of digits, you can use a catchy phrase or sequence that aligns with your brand, making all your marketing more effective and cohesive.

**How to Choose the Perfect Vanity Phone Number**

Selecting the right vanity number is crucial. Here’s how to find one that fits your brand perfectly:

1. **Identify Key Brand Elements:** Start by listing keywords that represent your brand and its offerings. These words will form the foundation of your search for the perfect number.
2. **Consider Your Customers:** Think about what would appeal to your target demographic. What words or phrases might resonate with them? For example, if you’re in the automotive industry, numbers including words like “AUTO” or “CARS” could be effective.
3. **Check Availability:** Once you have a list of potential numbers, check their availability. This can usually be done through phone service providers or websites specializing in vanity numbers.

**The Process of Buying Vanity Phone Numbers**

Purchasing a vanity number typically involves the following steps:

1. **Search for Availability:** Use tools provided by phone services or specialized websites to find available numbers.
2. **Evaluate the Options:** Once you find available numbers, evaluate them based on how closely they match your brand and how easy they are to remember.
3. **Complete the Purchase:** Buy your chosen number through the service provider. Make sure to understand all associated costs and setup requirements.

**Case Studies: Successful Brands with Vanity Numbers**

Many businesses have leveraged [vanity numbers](https://numberguy.com/ "vanity numbers") to great success. For instance, 1-800-FLOWERS made its number an integral part of its brand identity, making it nearly synonymous with flower delivery services. This number doesn’t just make calling easier; it reinforces the brand’s core business every time it’s dialed.

**Maintaining Your Vanity Number**

Maintaining the effectiveness of your vanity number involves ensuring it stays relevant and top-of-mind. Regularly incorporate it into advertising, both offline and online. Make sure it appears in all promotional materials and is featured prominently on your website and social media profiles.

**Alternatives to Vanity Numbers**

If a traditional vanity number doesn’t suit your needs, consider these alternatives:

- **Sequential Numbers:** Numbers like 123-4567 can be almost as memorable as word-based vanity numbers.
- **Repeat Numbers:** Sequences like 555-5555 are extremely easy to remember and can still provide some branding benefits.

**Tips for Negotiating the Best Deal**

When acquiring a vanity number, keep these tips in mind to secure the best deal:

- **Research Pricing:** Understand the going rates for vanity numbers to ensure you’re getting a fair price.
- **Be Flexible:** If your first choice isn’t available, be ready with alternatives that could work nearly as well.
- **Negotiate Terms:** Don’t just negotiate on price. Terms like transfer capabilities and bundled services can also be important.

**Frequently Asked Questions**

1. **What is the difference between a vanity and a toll-free number?**
    - A vanity number is a memorably arranged sequence of numbers, which can also be toll-free, but not all toll-free numbers are considered vanity numbers unless they spell out something distinctive or are otherwise memorable.
2. **Can I transfer my vanity phone number if I switch providers?**
    - Yes, in most cases, you can transfer your vanity phone number between providers. This process is known as “porting.”
3. **How much does a vanity phone number typically cost?**
    - The cost can vary widely depending on the uniqueness and memorability of the number. Basic vanity numbers may be quite affordable, while highly desirable sequences can command premium prices.
4. **Are there any ongoing costs associated with owning a vanity number?**
    - Yes, there will typically be recurring costs for line maintenance and the service plan associated with the number.
5. **How long does it take to activate a vanity phone number?**
    - Activation times can vary, but most numbers can be activated within a few business days once the purchase and setup are complete.

### Conclusion

Investing in a special or vanity phone number can offer significant benefits, from enhancing your brand’s memorability to improving marketing efficiency. Whether for business or personal branding, these numbers can be a valuable asset in your communications strategy. With the right approach, a special phone number can help your business stand out in a crowded marketplace. Ready to make your communication as unique as your brand? Start exploring your vanity number options today!

Area code 205 is located in Alabama and covers Birmingham, Tuscaloosa, and Hoover. It has a single overlay (659) that serves the same area. ## What time zone is area code 205?

The 205 area code is located in the Central timezone. The Central time zone is also known as America/Chicago. As of the last time this page was loaded. ## History

**Creation:** Area code 205 was put into service in 1947 and was one of the original 86 area codes, and it originally served the entire state of Alabama. 205 was split in 1995 creating the need to update some of the phone numbers to area code 334, and again in 1998 to create area code 256. In 2019, area code 659 was created and is currently an overlay to 205. It was the 1st area code in the state of Alabama. Alabama currently has 6 area codes. **New/recent overlays:** Area code 659 was recently added as on overaly to the 205 area code on November 12, 2019. **Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. Because the middle digit of the 205 area code is 0 and it was created prior to 1953, we can tell area code 205 originally served the entire state of Alabama. However, it not longer does. **Pulses:** Because area code 205 was created before the 1960s when touch tone dialing became more common, the number of pulses required on a rotary phone was still important. Area codes that required fewer pulses were faster to dial and were commonly prioritized for more populated areas. The 205 area code requires 2 + 10 + 5 = 17 pulses to dial. The 201 area code is located in the Eastern timezone. The Eastern time zone is also known as America/New\_York. As of the last time this page was loaded. ## History

In 2001, area code 551 was created and is currently an overlay to 201. It was the 1st area code in the state of New Jersey. New Jersey currently has 10 area codes. **Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. Because the middle digit of the 201 area code is 0 and it was created prior to 1953, we can tell area code 201 originally served the entire state of New Jersey. However, it not longer does. **Pulses:** Because area code 201 was created before the 1960s when touch tone dialing became more common, the number of pulses required on a rotary phone was still important. Area codes that required fewer pulses were faster to dial and were commonly prioritized for more populated areas. The 201 area code requires 2 + 10 + 1 = 13 pulses to dial. Area codes that required fewer pulses were faster to dial and were commonly prioritized for more populated areas. The 901 area code requires 9 + 10 + 1 = 20 pulses to dial. The 90 area codes created in the 5 years prior or the 5 years after area code 901 averaged 14.1 pulses indicating 901 was prioritized less than other area codes created about the same time. Without overlays, it was clear that a 7 digit number should be routed to the local area code. However, with overlays, multiple area codes can serve a single area which makes the area code for a 7 digit number ambiguous. Of the 469 area codes currently active, area code 901 is one of fewer than 71 that still allow 7 digit dialing for local calls. It was the 10th area code in the state of Pennsylvania. Pennsylvania currently has 15 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 412 area code as the numbers in 412 were being exhausted. **Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 - area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 862 is located in northern New Jersey and covers Newark, Paterson, Clifton, Passaic, and East Orange. It is an overlay for area code 973 and serves the same area. ## **What time zone is area code 862 ?**

The 862 area code is located in the Eastern timezone. The Eastern time zone is also known as America/New\_York. As of the last time this page was loaded. ## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 862 was put into service on December 29, 2001 and was the 309th area code in service. It was one of 26 area codes introduced in 2001. It was the 7th area code in the state of New Jersey. New Jersey currently has 10 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 973 area code as the numbers in 973 were being exhausted. **Middle digit :** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. When the 862 area code was created in 2001, it was the 160th area code without 0 or 1 as the middle digit. **Overlay :** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 - area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 862 is an overlay area code for area code 973. **Mnemonics :** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone's dialing pad. So, only area codes created in 1995 or later can have a mnemonic. The mnemonics for area code 862 include TMA, TMB, TMC, TNA, TNB, TNC, TOA, TOB, TOC, UMA, UMB, UMC, UNA, UNB, UNC, UOA, UOB, UOC, VMA, VMB, VMC, VNA, VNB, VNC, VOA, VOB, and VOC. **Creation:** Area code 848 was put into service on December 29, 2001 and was the 309th area code in service. It was one of 26 area codes introduced in 2001. It was the 7th area code in the state of New Jersey. New Jersey currently has 10 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 732 area code as the numbers in 732 were being exhausted. **Middle digit::** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. When the 848 area code was created in 2001, it was the 160th area code without 0 or 1 as the middle digit. **Overlay::** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 - area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 848 is an overlay area code for area code 732. **Mnemonics::** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone's dialing pad. So, only area codes created in 1995 or later can have a mnemonic. The 845 area code is located in the Eastern timezone. The Eastern time zone is also known as America/New\_York. As of the last time this page was loaded. ## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 845 was put into service on June 5, 2000 and was the 278th area code in service. It was one of 14 area codes introduced in 2000. In 2023, area code 329 was created and is currently an overlay to 845. It was the 13th area code in the state of New York. New York currently has 22 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 914 area code as the numbers in 914 were being exhausted. **New/recent overlays:** Area code 329 was recently added as on overaly to the 845 area code on March 24, 2023. **Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 - area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 845 is an overlay area code for area code 914. **Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone's dialing pad. So, only area codes created in 1995 or later can have a mnemonic. Without overlays, it was clear that a 7 digit number should be routed to the local area code. However, with overlays, multiple area codes can serve a single area which makes the area code for a 7 digit number ambiguous. At minimum, to support 7 digit dialing, an area code must not have an overlay and must not allocate numbers of the form 988-XXXX to avoid ambiguity with the 988 suicide prevention lifeline implemented in 2022-2023. **Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone's dialing pad. The 815 area code is located in the Central timezone. The Central time zone is also known as America/Chicago. As of the last time this page was loaded, the current time is 2:02am. ## **History**

Illinois currently has 17 area codes. **Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. Because the middle digit of the 815 area code is 1 and it was created prior to 1953, we can tell area code 815 never served the entire state of Illinois. **Pulses:** Because area code 815 was created before the 1960s when touch tone dialing became more common, the number of pulses required on a rotary phone was still important. Area codes that required fewer pulses were faster to dial and were commonly prioritized for more populated areas. The 815 area code requires 8 + 1 + 5 = 14 pulses to dial. **Creation:** Area code 779 was put into service on March 17, 2007 and was the 332nd area code in service. It was one of 3 area codes introduced in 2007. It was the 11th area code in the state of Illinois. Illinois currently has 17 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 815 area code as the numbers in 815 were being exhausted. **Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 - area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 779 is an overlay area code for area code 815. **Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone's dialing pad. Area code 773 serves most of Chicago, IL. It overlaps coverage areas with area code 872. ## **What time zone is area code 773?**

The 773 area code is located in the Central timezone. The Central time zone is also known as America/Chicago. As of the last time this page was loaded. ## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 773 was put into service on October 12, 1996 and was the 182nd area code in service. It was one of 21 area codes introduced in 1996. It was the 9th area code in the state of Illinois. Illinois currently has 17 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 312 area code as the numbers in 312 were being exhausted. **Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. When the 773 area code was created in 1996, it was the 33rd area code without 0 or 1 as the middle digit. **Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 - area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 773 is an overlay area code for area code 312. **Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone's dialing pad. So, only area codes created in 1995 or later can have a mnemonic. The mnemonics for area code 773 include PPD, PPE, PPF, PQD, PQE, PQF, PRD, PRE, PRF, PSD, PSE, PSF, QPD, QPE, QPF, QQD, QQE, QQF, QRD, QRE, QRF, QSD, QSE, QSF, RPD, RPE, RPF, RQD, RQE, RQF, RRD, RRE, RRF, RSD, RSE, RSF, SPD, SPE, SPF, SQD, SQE, SQF, SRD, SRE, SRF, SSD, SSE, and SSF. **Creation:** Area code 769 was put into service on March 14, 2005 and was the 326th area code in service. It was one of 2 area codes introduced in 2005. It was the 4th area code in the state of Mississippi. Mississippi currently has 4 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 601 area code as the numbers in 601 were being exhausted. **Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 - area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 769 is an overlay area code for area code 601. **Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone's dialing pad. So, only area codes created in 1995 or later can have a mnemonic. It was the 8th area code in the state of Georgia. Georgia currently has 10 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 706 area code as the numbers in 706 were being exhausted. **Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 - area codes that would serve the same geographic area. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. Area code 743 is an overlay area code for area code 336. **Pulses:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone's dialing pad. Area code 726 serves San Antonio, TX and the surrounding areas. It is an overlay for area code 210 and serves the same area. ## **What time zone is area code 726 ?**

The 726 area code is located in the Central timezone. The Central time zone is also known as America/Chicago. As of the last time this page was loaded. ## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 726 was put into service on October 23, 2017 and was the 401st area code in service. It was one of 9 area codes introduced in 2017. It was the 27th area code in the state of Texas. Texas currently has 28 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 210 area code as the numbers in 210 were being exhausted. **Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 404 area code as the numbers in 404 were being exhausted. **Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 - area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 706 is an overlay area code for area code 404. **Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone's dialing pad. When the 728 area code was created in 2023, it was the 300th area code without 0 or 1 as the middle digit. **Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 - area codes that would serve the same geographic area. It was the 6th area code in the state of Alabama. Alabama currently has 6 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 205 area code as the numbers in 205 were being exhausted. **Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. **Creation:** Area code 646 was put into service on July 1, 1999 and was the 262nd area code in service. It was one of 23 area codes introduced in 1999. It was the 10th area code in the state of New York. New York currently has 22 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 212 area code as the numbers in 212 were being exhausted. **Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 - area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 646 is an overlay area code for area code 212. **Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone's dialing pad. So, only area codes created in 1995 or later can have a mnemonic. Without overlays, it was clear that a 7 digit number should be routed to the local area code. However, with overlays, multiple area codes can serve a single area which makes the area code for a 7 digit number ambiguous. Area codes that required fewer pulses were faster to dial and were commonly prioritized for more populated areas. The 515 area code requires 5 + 1 + 5 = 11 pulses to dial. Area codes that required fewer pulses were faster to dial and were commonly prioritized for more populated areas. The 501 area code requires 5 + 10 + 1 = 16 pulses to dial. **Creation:** Area code 475 was put into service on December 12, 2009 and was the 345th area code in service. It was one of 8 area codes introduced in 2009. It was the 3rd area code in the state of Connecticut. Connecticut currently has 4 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 203 area code as the numbers in 203 were being exhausted. **Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 - area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 475 is an overlay area code for area code 203. **Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone's dialing pad. ## **Where is area code 326 ?**

Area code 326 serves southwestern Ohio except the Cincinnati metro area. It includes the cities of Dayton, Springfield, and Kettering. It is an overlay for area code 937 and serves the same area.

## **What time zone is area code 326 ?**

The 326 area code is located in the Eastern timezone. The Eastern time zone is also known as America/New\_York. As of the last time this page was loaded.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 326 was put into service on March 8, 2020 and was the 413th area code in service. It was one of 3 area codes introduced in 2020. It was the 13th area code in the state of Ohio. Ohio currently has 15 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 937 area code as the numbers in 937 were being exhausted.

**Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 – area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 326 is an overlay area code for area code 937

**Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone’s dialing pad. So, only area codes created in 1995 or later can have a mnemonic. The mnemonics for area code 326 include DAM, DAN, DAO, DBM, DBN, DBO, DCM, DCN, DCO, EAM, EAN, EAO, EBM, EBN, EBO, ECM, ECN, ECO, FAM, FAN, FAO, FBM, FBN, FBO, FCM, FCN, and FCO. ## **Where is area code 323?**

Area code 323 serves part of Los Angeles, CA and the surrounding areas. It is an overlay for area code 213 and serves the same area.

## **What time zone is area code 323?**

The 323 area code is located in the Pacific timezone. The Pacific time zone is also known as America/Los\_Angeles. As of the last time this page was loaded.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 323 was put into service on June 13, 1998 and was the 240th area code in service. It was one of 21 area codes introduced in 1998. It was the 21st area code in the state of California. California currently has 38 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 213 area code as the numbers in 213 were being exhausted.

**New/recent overlays:** Though future plans may change, area code 738 has been proposed as a possible overlay for area code 323. The new overlay is expected to go in service on November 1, 2024.

**Overlay:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone’s dialing pad. So, only area codes created in 1995 or later can have a mnemonic. The mnemonics for area code 323 include DAD, DAE, DAF, DBD, DBE, DBF, DCD, DCE, DCF, EAD, EAE, EAF, EBD, EBE, EBF, ECD, ECE, ECF, FAD, FAE, FAF, FBD, FBE, FBF, FCD, FCE, and FCF. Let us know if one of these mnemonics fits area code 323 so we can feature it.

**Mnemonics:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 – area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 323 is an overlay area code for area code 213.

## **History**

**Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 – area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 321 is an overlay area code for area code 407.

**7 digit dialing:** Before area code overlays were made common in the 1990s, a local phone number could be dialed without dialing the area code – just dialing the last 7 digits of the phone number. Without overlays, it was clear that a 7 digit number should be routed to the local area code. However, with overlays, multiple area codes can serve a single area which makes the area code for a 7 digit number ambiguous. Of the 469 area codes currently active, area code 320 is one of fewer than 71 that still allow 7 digit dialing for local calls. At minimum, to support 7 digit dialing, an area code must not have an overlay and must not allocate numbers of the form 988-XXXX to avoid ambiguity with the 988 suicide prevention lifeline implemented in 2022-2023

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 319 was put into service in 1947 and was one of the original 86 area codes, and it originally served the eastern third of Iowa. 319 was split in 2001 creating the need to update some of the phone numbers to area code 563. It was the 1st area code in the state of Iowa. Iowa currently has 5 area codes.

**Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. Because the middle digit of the 319 area code is 1 and it was created prior to 1953, we can tell area code 319 never served the entire state of Iowa.

**Pulses:** Because area code 319 was created before the 1960s when touch tone dialing became more common, the number of pulses required on a rotary phone was still important. Area codes that required fewer pulses were faster to dial and were commonly prioritized for more populated areas. The 319 area code requires 3 + 1 + 9 = 13 pulses to dial. The 90 area codes created in the 5 years prior or the 5 years after area code 319 averaged 14.1 pulses indicating 319 was prioritized more than other area codes created about the same time. The 469 currently active area codes require pulses that range from 5 to 29 and average 16.3.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 318 was put into service in 1957 and was the 104th area code in service. It was one of 10 area codes introduced in 1957. 318 was split in 1999 creating the need to update some of the phone numbers to area code 337. It was the 2nd area code in the state of Louisiana. Louisiana currently has 5 area codes.

**New/recent overlays:** Though future plans may change, area code 457 has been proposed as a possible overlay for area code 318. The new overlay is expected to go in service on September 25, 2025.

**Pulses:** Because area code 318 was created before the 1960s when touch tone dialing became more common, the number of pulses required on a rotary phone was still important. Area codes that required fewer pulses were faster to dial and were commonly prioritized for more populated areas. The 318 area code requires 3 + 1 + 8 = 12 pulses to dial. The 28 area codes created in the 5 years prior or the 5 years after area code 318 averaged 20.6 pulses indicating 318 was prioritized more than other area codes created about the same time. The 469 currently active area codes require pulses that range from 5 to 29 and average 16.3.

**7 digit dialing:** Before area code overlays were made common in the 1990s, a local phone number could be dialed without dialing the area code – just dialing the last 7 digits of the phone number. Without overlays, it was clear that a 7 digit number should be routed to the local area code. However, with overlays, multiple area codes can serve a single area which makes the area code for a 7 digit number ambiguous. Of the 469 area codes currently active, area code 318 is one of fewer than 71 that still allow 7 digit dialing for local calls. At minimum, to support 7 digit dialing, an area code must not have an overlay and must not allocate numbers of the form 988-XXXX to avoid ambiguity with the 988 suicide prevention lifeline implemented in 2022-2023.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 317 was put into service in 1947 and was one of the original 86 area codes, and it originally served the northern two-thirds of Indiana including Indianapolis. 317 was split in 1997 creating the need to update some of the phone numbers to area code 765. In 2016, area code 463 was created and is currently an overlay to 317. It was the 1st area code in the state of Indiana. Indiana currently has 8 area codes.

**Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. Because the middle digit of the 317 area code is 1 and it was created prior to 1953, we can tell area code 317 never served the entire state of Indiana.

**Pulses:** Because area code 317 was created before the 1960s when touch tone dialing became more common, the number of pulses required on a rotary phone was still important. Area codes that required fewer pulses were faster to dial and were commonly prioritized for more populated areas. The 317 area code requires 3 + 1 + 7 = 11 pulses to dial. The 90 area codes created in the 5 years prior or the 5 years after area code 317 averaged 14.1 pulses indicating 317 was prioritized more than other area codes created about the same time. The 469 currently active area codes require pulses that range from 5 to 29 and average 16.3.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 314 was put into service in 1947 and was one of the original 86 area codes, and it originally served eastern Missouri including St. Louis. 314 was split in 1996 creating the need to update some of the phone numbers to area code 573, and again in 1999 to create area code 636. In 2022, area code 557 was created and is currently an overlay to 314. It was the 1st area code in the state of Missouri. Missouri currently has 9 area codes.

**New/recent overlays:** Area code 557 was recently added as on overaly to the 314 area code on August 12, 2022.

**Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. Because the middle digit of the 314 area code is 1 and it was created prior to 1953, we can tell area code 314 never served the entire state of Missouri.

**Pulses:** Because area code 314 was created before the 1960s when touch tone dialing became more common, the number of pulses required on a rotary phone was still important. Area codes that required fewer pulses were faster to dial and were commonly prioritized for more populated areas. The 314 area code requires 3 + 1 + 4 = 8 pulses to dial. The 90 area codes created in the 5 years prior or the 5 years after area code 314 averaged 14.1 pulses indicating 314 was prioritized more than other area codes created about the same time. The 469 currently active area codes require pulses that range from 5 to 29 and average 16.3. Only 10 area codes require fewer pulses (212, 213, 312, 231, 321, 214, 313, 412, 331, and 223) than area code 314.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 313 was put into service in 1947 and was one of the original 86 area codes, and it originally served southeast Michigan including Detroit. 313 was split in 1997 creating the need to update some of the phone numbers to area code 734. It was the 1st area code in the state of Michigan. Michigan currently has 12 area codes.

**New/recent overlays:** Though future plans may change, area code 679 has been proposed as a possible overlay for area code 313. The new overlay is expected to go in service on November 7, 2025.

**Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. Because the middle digit of the 313 area code is 1 and it was created prior to 1953, we can tell area code 313 never served the entire state of Michigan.

**Pulses:** Because area code 313 was created before the 1960s when touch tone dialing became more common, the number of pulses required on a rotary phone was still important. Area codes that required fewer pulses were faster to dial and were commonly prioritized for more populated areas. The 313 area code requires 3 + 1 + 3 = 7 pulses to dial. The 90 area codes created in the 5 years prior or the 5 years after area code 313 averaged 14.1 pulses indicating 313 was prioritized more than other area codes created about the same time. The 469 currently active area codes require pulses that range from 5 to 29 and average 16.3. Only 5 area codes require fewer pulses (212, 213, 312, 231, and 321) than area code 313.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 312 was put into service in 1947 and was one of the original 86 area codes, and it originally served the Chicago metropolitan area. 312 was split in 1996 creating the need to update some of the phone numbers to area code 773. In 2009, area code 872 was created and is currently an overlay to 312 and 773. It was the 1st area code in the state of Illinois. Illinois currently has 17 area codes.

**Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. Because the middle digit of the 312 area code is 1 and it was created prior to 1953, we can tell area code 312 never served the entire state of Illinois.

**Pulses:** Because area code 312 was created before the 1960s when touch tone dialing became more common, the number of pulses required on a rotary phone was still important. Area codes that required fewer pulses were faster to dial and were commonly prioritized for more populated areas. The 312 area code requires 3 + 1 + 2 = 6 pulses to dial. The 90 area codes created in the 5 years prior or the 5 years after area code 312 averaged 14.1 pulses indicating 312 was prioritized more than other area codes created about the same time. The 469 currently active area codes require pulses that range from 5 to 29 and average 16.3. Only 1 area code requires fewer pulses (212) than area code 312.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 309 was put into service in 1957 and was the 104th area code in service. It was one of 10 area codes introduced in 1957. In 2023, area code 861 was created and is currently an overlay to 309. It was the 5th area code in the state of Illinois. Illinois currently has 17 area codes

**New/recent overlays:** Area code 861 was recently added as on overaly to the 309 area code on February 24, 2023.

**Pulses:** Because area code 309 was created before the 1960s when touch tone dialing became more common, the number of pulses required on a rotary phone was still important. Area codes that required fewer pulses were faster to dial and were commonly prioritized for more populated areas. The 309 area code requires 3 + 10 + 9 = 22 pulses to dial. The 28 area codes created in the 5 years prior or the 5 years after area code 309 averaged 20.6 pulses indicating 309 was prioritized less than other area codes created about the same time. The 469 currently active area codes require pulses that range from 5 to 29 and average 16.3. Only 49 area codes require more pulses than area code 309.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 308 was put into service in 1955 and was the 100th area code in service. It was one of 4 area codes introduced in 1955. It was the 2nd area code in the state of Nebraska. Nebraska currently has 3 area codes.

**Pulses:** Because area code 308 was created before the 1960s when touch tone dialing became more common, the number of pulses required on a rotary phone was still important. Area codes that required fewer pulses were faster to dial and were commonly prioritized for more populated areas. The 308 area code requires 3 + 10 + 8 = 21 pulses to dial. The 29 area codes created in the 5 years prior or the 5 years after area code 308 averaged 19.9 pulses indicating 308 was prioritized less than other area codes created about the same time. The 469 currently active area codes require pulses that range from 5 to 29 and average 16.3.

**7 digit dialing:** Before area code overlays were made common in the 1990s, a local phone number could be dialed without dialing the area code – just dialing the last 7 digits of the phone number. Without overlays, it was clear that a 7 digit number should be routed to the local area code. However, with overlays, multiple area codes can serve a single area which makes the area code for a 7 digit number ambiguous. Of the 469 area codes currently active, area code 308 is one of fewer than 71 that still allow 7 digit dialing for local calls. At minimum, to support 7 digit dialing, an area code must not have an overlay and must not allocate numbers of the form 988-XXXX to avoid ambiguity with the 988 suicide prevention lifeline implemented in 2022-2023.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 307 was put into service in 1947 and was one of the original 86 area codes, and it originally served the entire state of Wyoming. It is currently the only area code in the state of Wyoming. Wyoming is one of only 11 states that still have only a single area code.

**Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. Because the middle digit of the 307 area code is 0 and it was created prior to 1953, we can tell area code 307 originally served the entire state of Wyoming. It is one of only 15 of the original 86 area codes that are still used for an entire state.

**Pulses:** Because area code 307 was created before the 1960s when touch tone dialing became more common, the number of pulses required on a rotary phone was still important. Area codes that required fewer pulses were faster to dial and were commonly prioritized for more populated areas. The 307 area code requires 3 + 10 + 7 = 20 pulses to dial. The 90 area codes created in the 5 years prior or the 5 years after area code 307 averaged 14.1 pulses indicating 307 was prioritized less than other area codes created about the same time. The 469 currently active area codes require pulses that range from 5 to 29 and average 16.3.

**7 digit dialing:** Before area code overlays were made common in the 1990s, a local phone number could be dialed without dialing the area code – just dialing the last 7 digits of the phone number. Without overlays, it was clear that a 7 digit number should be routed to the local area code. However, with overlays, multiple area codes can serve a single area which makes the area code for a 7 digit number ambiguous. Of the 469 area codes currently active, area code 307 is one of fewer than 71 that still allow 7 digit dialing for local calls. At minimum, to support 7 digit dialing, an area code must not have an overlay and must not allocate numbers of the form 988-XXXX to avoid ambiguity with the 988 suicide prevention lifeline implemented in 2022-2023.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 303 was put into service in 1947 and was one of the original 86 area codes, and it originally served the entire state of Colorado. 303 was split in 1995 creating the need to update some of the phone numbers to area code 970. In 1998, area code 720 was created and is currently an overlay to 303. In 2022, area code 983 was created and is currently an overlay to 303. It was the 1st area code in the state of Colorado. Colorado currently has 5 area codes.

**Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. Because the middle digit of the 303 area code is 0 and it was created prior to 1953, we can tell area code 303 originally served the entire state of Colorado. However, it not longer does.

**Pulses:** Because area code 303 was created before the 1960s when touch tone dialing became more common, the number of pulses required on a rotary phone was still important. Area codes that required fewer pulses were faster to dial and were commonly prioritized for more populated areas. The 303 area code requires 3 + 10 + 3 = 16 pulses to dial. The 90 area codes created in the 5 years prior or the 5 years after area code 303 averaged 14.1 pulses indicating 303 was prioritized less than other area codes created about the same time. The 469 currently active area codes require pulses that range from 5 to 29 and average 16.3.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 302 was put into service in 1947 and was one of the original 86 area codes, and it originally served the entire state of Delaware. It is currently the only area code in the state of Delaware. Delaware is one of only 11 states that still have only a single area code.

**Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. Because the middle digit of the 302 area code is 0 and it was created prior to 1953, we can tell area code 302 originally served the entire state of Delaware. It is one of only 15 of the original 86 area codes that are still used for an entire state.

**Pulses:** Because area code 302 was created before the 1960s when touch tone dialing became more common, the number of pulses required on a rotary phone was still important. Area codes that required fewer pulses were faster to dial and were commonly prioritized for more populated areas. The 302 area code requires 3 + 10 + 2 = 15 pulses to dial. The 90 area codes created in the 5 years prior or the 5 years after area code 302 averaged 14.1 pulses indicating 302 was prioritized less than other area codes created about the same time. The 469 currently active area codes require pulses that range from 5 to 29 and average 16.3.

## **Where is area code 283 ?**

Area code 283 serves the Cincinnati, OH metro area. It includes the cities of Cincinnati, Hamilton, and Middletown. It is an overlay for area code 513 and serves the same area.

## **What time zone is area code 283 ?**

The 283 area code is located in the Eastern timezone. The Eastern time zone is also known as America/New\_York. As of the last time this page was loaded.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 283 was put into service on April 28, 2023 and was the 451st area code in service. It was one of 16 area codes introduced in 2023. It was the 14th area code in the state of Ohio. Ohio currently has 15 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 513 area code as the numbers in 513 were being exhausted.

**Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 – area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 283 is an overlay area code for area code 513.

**Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone’s dialing pad. So, only area codes created in 1995 or later can have a mnemonic. ## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 281 was put into service on November 2, 1996 and was the 184th area code in service. It was one of 21 area codes introduced in 1996. It was the 11th area code in the state of Texas. Texas currently has 28 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 713 area code as the numbers in 713 were being exhausted.

**New/recent overlays:** Though future plans may change, area code 621 has been proposed as a possible overlay for area code 281. The new overlay is expected to go in service on January 23, 2025.

**Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. When the 281 area code was created in 1996, it was the 35th area code without 0 or 1 as the middle digit.

**Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 – area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 281 is an overlay area code for area code 713.

## **Where is area code 279?**

Area code 279 serves Sacramento, CA and the surrounding areas. It is an overlay for area code 916 and serves the same area.

## **What time zone is area code 279?**

The 279 area code is located in the Pacific timezone. The Pacific time zone is also known as America/Los\_Angeles. As of the last time this page was loaded, the current time is 2:30am.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 279 was put into service on March 10, 2018 and was the 403rd area code in service. It was one of 6 area codes introduced in 2018. It was the 33rd area code in the state of California. California currently has 38 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 916 area code as the numbers in 916 were being exhausted.

**Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 – area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 279 is an overlay area code for area code 916.

**Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone’s dialing pad. So, only area codes created in 1995 or later can have a mnemonic. The mnemonics for area code 279 include APW, APX, APY, APZ, AQW, AQX, AQY, AQZ, ARW, ARX, ARY, ARZ, ASW, ASX, ASY, ASZ, BPW, BPX, BPY, BPZ, BQW, BQX, BQY, BQZ, BRW, BRX, BRY, BRZ, BSW, BSX, BSY, BSZ, CPW, CPX, CPY, CPZ, CQW, CQX, CQY, CQZ, CRW, CRX, CRY, CRZ, CSW, CSX, CSY, and CSZ. Let us know if one of these mnemonics fits area code 279 so we can feature it.

## **Where is area code 272?**

Area code 272 is located in northeastern Pennsylvania and covers Scranton, Wilkes-Barre, and Williamsport. It is an overlay for area code 570 and serves the same area.

## **What time zone is area code 272?**

The 272 area code is located in the Eastern timezone. The Eastern time zone is also known as America/New\_York. As of the last time this page was loaded.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 272 was put into service on October 21, 2013 and was the 371st area code in service. It was one of 8 area codes introduced in 2013. It was the 11th area code in the state of Pennsylvania. Pennsylvania currently has 15 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 570 area code as the numbers in 570 were being exhausted.

**Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 – area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 272 is an overlay area code for area code 570.

**Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone’s dialing pad. So, only area codes created in 1995 or later can have a mnemonic. The mnemonics for area code 272 include APA, APB, APC, AQA, AQB, AQC, ARA, ARB, ARC, ASA, ASB, ASC, BPA, BPB, BPC, BQA, BQB, BQC, BRA, BRB, BRC, BSA, BSB, BSC, CPA, CPB, CPC, CQA, CQB, CQC, CRA, CRB, CRC, CSA, CSB, and CSC. ## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 269 was put into service on July 13, 2002 and was the 319th area code in service. It was one of 9 area codes introduced in 2002. It was the 11th area code in the state of Michigan. Michigan currently has 12 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 616 area code as the numbers in 616 were being exhausted.

**Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. When the 269 area code was created in 2002, it was the 170th area code without 0 or 1 as the middle digit.

**7 digit dialing:** Before area code overlays were made common in the 1990s, a local phone number could be dialed without dialing the area code – just dialing the last 7 digits of the phone number. Without overlays, it was clear that a 7 digit number should be routed to the local area code. However, with overlays, multiple area codes can serve a single area which makes the area code for a 7 digit number ambiguous. Of the 469 area codes currently active, area code 269 is one of fewer than 71 that still allow 7 digit dialing for local calls. At minimum, to support 7 digit dialing, an area code must not have an overlay and must not allocate numbers of the form 988-XXXX to avoid ambiguity with the 988 suicide prevention lifeline implemented in 2022-2023.

**Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone’s dialing pad. So, only area codes created in 1995 or later can have a mnemonic. The mnemonics for area code 269 include AMW, AMX, AMY, AMZ, ANW, ANX, ANY, ANZ, AOW, AOX, AOY, AOZ, BMW, BMX, BMY, BMZ, BNW, BNX, BNY, BNZ, BOW, BOX, BOY, BOZ, CMW, CMX, CMY, CMZ, CNW, CNX, CNY, CNZ, COW, COX, COY, and COZ. When the 268 area code was created in 1996, it was the 21st area code without 0 or 1 as the middle digit.

**7 digit dialing:** Before area code overlays were made common in the 1990s, a local phone number could be dialed without dialing the area code – just dialing the last 7 digits of the phone number. Without overlays, it was clear that a 7 digit number should be routed to the local area code. However, with overlays, multiple area codes can serve a single area which makes the area code for a 7 digit number ambiguous. ## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 260 was put into service on January 15, 2002 and was the 314th area code in service. It was one of 9 area codes introduced in 2002. It was the 5th area code in the state of Indiana. Indiana currently has 8 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 219 area code as the numbers in 219 were being exhausted.

**7 digit dialing:** Before area code overlays were made common in the 1990s, a local phone number could be dialed without dialing the area code – just dialing the last 7 digits of the phone number. Without overlays, it was clear that a 7 digit number should be routed to the local area code. However, with overlays, multiple area codes can serve a single area which makes the area code for a 7 digit number ambiguous. Of the 467 area codes currently active, area code 260 is one of fewer than 71 that still allow 7 digit dialing for local calls. At minimum, to support 7 digit dialing, an area code must not have an overlay and must not allocate numbers of the form 988-XXXX to avoid ambiguity with the 988 suicide prevention lifeline implemented in 2022-2023.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 254 was put into service on May 25, 1997 and was the 194th area code in service. It was one of 43 area codes introduced in 1997. It was the 12th area code in the state of Texas. Texas currently has 28 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 817 area code as the numbers in 817 were being exhausted.

**Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. When the 254 area code was created in 1997, it was the 45th area code without 0 or 1 as the middle digit.

**Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone’s dialing pad. So, only area codes created in 1995 or later can have a mnemonic. ## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 253 was put into service on April 27, 1997 and was the 190th area code in service. It was one of 43 area codes introduced in 1997. It was the 4th area code in the state of Washington. Washington currently has 6 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 206 area code as the numbers in 206 were being exhausted.

**Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. When the 253 area code was created in 1997, it was the 41st area code without 0 or 1 as the middle digit.

**Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone’s dialing pad. So, only area codes created in 1995 or later can have a mnemonic. The mnemonics for area code 253 include AJD, AJE, AJF, AKD, AKE, AKF, ALD, ALE, ALF, BJD, BJE, BJF, BKD, BKE, BKF, BLD, BLE, BLF, CJD, CJE, CJF, CKD, CKE, CKF, CLD, CLE, and CLF. ## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 252 was put into service on March 22, 1998 and was the 232nd area code in service. It was one of 21 area codes introduced in 1998. It was the 5th area code in the state of North Carolina. North Carolina currently has 10 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 919 area code as the numbers in 919 were being exhausted.

**7 digit dialing:** Before area code overlays were made common in the 1990s, a local phone number could be dialed without dialing the area code – just dialing the last 7 digits of the phone number. Without overlays, it was clear that a 7 digit number should be routed to the local area code. However, with overlays, multiple area codes can serve a single area which makes the area code for a 7 digit number ambiguous. Of the 467 area codes currently active, area code 252 is one of fewer than 71 that still allow 7 digit dialing for local calls. At minimum, to support 7 digit dialing, an area code must not have an overlay and must not allocate numbers of the form 988-XXXX to avoid ambiguity with the 988 suicide prevention lifeline implemented in 2022-2023.

**Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone’s dialing pad. So, only area codes created in 1995 or later can have a mnemonic. ## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 250 was put into service on October 19, 1996 and was the 183rd area code in service. It was one of 21 area codes introduced in 1996. It was the 2nd area code in the province of British Columbia. British Columbia currently has 5 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 604 area code as the numbers in 604 were being exhausted.

**New/recent overlays:** Though future plans may change, area code 257 has been proposed as a possible overlay for area code 250. The new overlay is expected to go in service on May 24, 2025.

**Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire province while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a province. When the 250 area code was created in 1996, it was the 34th area code without 0 or 1 as the middle digit.

**Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 – area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 250 is an overlay area code for area code 604.

## **Where is area code 249?**

Area code 249 serves northeastern Ontario, Canada including Sudbury. It is an overlay for area code 705 and serves the same area.

## **What time zone is area code 249?**

The 249 area code is located in the Eastern timezone. The Eastern time zone is also known as America/New\_York. As of the last time this page was loaded.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 249 was put into service on March 19, 2011 and was the 354th area code in service. It was one of 5 area codes introduced in 2011. It was the 11th area code in the province of Ontario. Ontario currently has 18 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 705 area code as the numbers in 705 were being exhausted.

**New/recent overlays:** Area code 683 was recently added as on overaly to the 249 area code on June 18, 2022.

**Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 – area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 249 is an overlay area code for area code 705.

**Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone’s dialing pad. So, only area codes created in 1995 or later can have a mnemonic. The mnemonics for area code 249 include AGW, AGX, AGY, AGZ, AHW, AHX, AHY, AHZ, AIW, AIX, AIY, AIZ, BGW, BGX, BGY, BGZ, BHW, BHX, BHY, BHZ, BIW, BIX, BIY, BIZ, CGW, CGX, CGY, CGZ, CHW, CHX, CHY, CHZ, CIW, CIX, CIY, and CIZ. ## **Where is area code 248?**

Area code 248 is located in Michigan and covers Troy, Farmington Hills, Southfield, Rochester Hills, and Pontiac. It has a single overlay (947) that serves the same area.

## **History**

**Creation:** Area code 248 was put into service on May 10, 1997 and was the 193rd area code in service. It was one of 43 area codes introduced in 1997. In 2002, area code 947 was created and is currently an overlay to 248. It was the 6th area code in the state of Michigan. Michigan currently has 12 area codes. It was created to relieve the pressure on the 810 area code as the numbers in 810 were being exhausted.

**Middle digit:** Until 1953, the middle digit was restricted to either a 0 or a 1 where a zero indicated that the area code covered the entire state while a 1 indicated that the area code served only a portion of a state. When the 248 area code was created in 1997, it was the 44th area code without 0 or 1 as the middle digit.

**Overlay:** Prior to 1992, each area code served a geographic area and that geographic area had only a single area code. If the phone numbers available for an area code were nearly exhausted, the existing area code and geographic area would be split. However, the North American Number Plan Administrator (NANPA) started to create overlay area codes in 1992 – area codes that would serve the same geographic area. Area code 248 is an overlay area code for area code 810.

**Mnemonics:** Prior to 1995, the middle digit of area codes was restricted to a 0 or 1 which do not correspond to a letter on a phone’s dialing pad. So, only area codes created in 1995 or later can have a mnemonic. The mnemonics for area code 248 include AGT, AGU, AGV, AHT, AHU, AHV, AIT, AIU, AIV, BGT, BGU, BGV, BHT, BHU, BHV, BIT, BIU, BIV, CGT, CGU, CGV, CHT, CHU, CHV, CIT, CIU, and CIV.
